orientation: Scribe is documentation and workflow-capture software that turns actions taken in applications into step-by-step how-to guides an IT team can share.

setup_conditions: Browser-based capture and guide generation is what the free Basic plan covers (E1)
Capturing processes in desktop applications requires a Pro or Enterprise account (E5)
All members of one Scribe team must sit on the same plan tier, and upgrading a team upgrades its members unless a separate team is created (E7, E6)
unverified_requirements: Step captures include screenshots of each step
Procedures are kept current when the underlying systems change
Captured procedures are reusable as structured context for internal AI tools
decision_gaps: Does Scribe's public documentation state that each captured step includes a screenshot, and on which plans?
Does Scribe document a mechanism for re-capturing or updating an existing guide when the underlying system changes?

unverified_requirement_basis.Captured procedures are reusable as stru: reused as training or as structured context for internal AI tools

defining_need_fit.caveat: Automatic capture into step-by-step guides and automatic redaction are documented (E12, E19, E22), but the selected evidence does not establish screenshot capture, any update-on-change mechanism, or an AI-context output format, and desktop-app capture is gated to Pro/Enterprise (E5).
defining_need_fit.why: Scribe documents automatic conversion of work already done into shareable step-by-step guides, which covers the capture-and-scale component of the need while three of its stated conditions remain unestablished by the selected evidence.

first_email_scope.request: Write exactly one email. Introduce our product to a new buyer with one clear next step.
first_email_scope.workflow: On the free Basic plan the buyer can, in the browser and without purchase, generate a how-to guide for one IT procedure they currently carry in their head, and Scribe's Autocapture can turn work already performed into such guides automatically, with sensitive data automatically redacted during capture.
setup_conditions: Free Basic plan covers browser-based guide generation only (E1)
Capturing processes in desktop applications requires Pro or Enterprise (E5)
Team-level plan tiers apply if the buyer later adds teammates (E7, E6)
excluded_promises: No claim that steps are captured as screenshots
No claim that guides stay current when systems change
No claim that output is usable as structured context for internal AI tools
No claim of zero disruption, headcount reduction, growth or replacement of an incumbent tool
No claim about time saved or mistakes avoided for this buyer

ranked_relevance.why: Autocapture is the documented mechanism that turns work already performed into step-by-step guides, which is the core of the stated documentation task.
The free Basic plan documents browser-based guide generation, which is a next action available without procurement.
States how capture behaves with sensitive data, which matters when IT screens are recorded.
Quantifies the redaction mechanism at 150 categories of PII, PHI and PCI.
Compliance posture and fine-grained workspace permissions are the documented controls an internal IT buyer reviews before sharing captured procedures.
Names the documented exception that desktop capture is Pro/Enterprise only, which bounds what the free next step covers.
Pro Team pricing from 5 seats is the documented path once a team rather than one person documents procedures.
Mixed-tier teams are not allowed, which materially shapes how an IT team would roll this out.
Upgrading a Pro plan upgrades the whole team unless a separate team is created, a condition any team-level decision must preserve.
Broader compliance list supports the security review an internal IT operations buyer performs.
Custom Enterprise pricing via demo is the documented later route, not the next step for an unqualified first contact.
Pro Personal is framed for solo consultants rather than a mid-size to large IT operations team.
Enterprise-only auto-redaction overlaps the broader redaction facts and adds a tier condition not needed for this draft.
Enterprise SSO is relevant only after a procurement conversation this first email does not open.
A named enterprise customer's endorsement is a licensing opinion, not a description of what the product does.
An L&D specialist's speed claim is a customer opinion from a different function and its employer is unnamed.
A marketing headline user count with no defined measurement is weak with a technical internal-IT buyer.
Unattributed 2025 survey multiple with no methodology invites challenge from this buyer.
Unattributed survey percentage about fewer mistakes has no stated baseline.
35 hours saved per person per month is an unattributed aggregate that would read as a headcount promise the user never requested.
AI agent performance gain has no methodology or baseline and the AI-context requirement is itself unverified here.
An AI roadmap timeline is unrelated to the documentation task this buyer performs.
Education discount requires a .edu address, which this organization type does not have.
Nonprofit discount requires 501(c)(3) proof, outside this audience's stated organization type.

problem_fits.caveat: The mechanism documents automatic conversion of completed work into guides, but the problem itself rests on a single 2019 forum thread about technology-company staff whose present applicability is uncorroborated, and no selected evidence shows documentation becoming a first-class deliverable.
problem_fits.why: Autocapture addresses the capture half of undocumented tribal knowledge without evidencing any change in how teams prioritise documentation.

segment_objections.objection: Most of our procedures run in desktop tools and system consoles, not a browser, so a free browser plan will not capture them.
segment_objections.answer: Browser capture is what the free Basic plan covers, and capturing processes in desktop applications is a Pro or Enterprise feature.

segment_objections.objection: IT screens show credentials, user records and ticket data, so recording them creates an exposure we cannot approve.
segment_objections.answer: Scribe states that sensitive data is automatically redacted during capture across 150 categories of PII, PHI and PCI, and that it is SOC 2 Type II, HIPAA, FERPA and GDPR compliant with fine-grained workspace permissions.
